verdict.rationale: Paddle's own docs include step-by-step checkout guides (overlay checkout with "minimal frontend coding required", plus inline checkout), four official server-side SDKs (Node.js, Python, Go, PHP), a sandbox for testing, and a Next.js starter kit that ends in a working subscription app, so the core of a docs-driven payment integration is there. The specific promises of the story are not shown in the evidence: nothing documents per-language copy-paste code snippets, and no hands-on report confirms a working flow within a day. Missing for 10: evidence of copy-paste code samples per language in the guides, independent or hands-on corroboration of under-a-day time-to-integration, and coverage of languages beyond the four server SDKs and JavaScript.

support.subject: As a developer, I can integrate a working payment flow from the docs alone in under a day, with copy-paste examples in my language

citations.quote: Overlay checkout lets you present customers with an overlay that handles all parts of the checkout process — minimal frontend coding required.
We support four official server-side SDKs: Node.js, Python, Go, and PHP.
By the end, you'll have a working three-tier subscription app integrated with Supabase for auth and Paddle webhooks for syncing customer data.
Sandbox is a separate Paddle environment for building and testing your integration without affecting real data or accepting real payments.
Add a checkout to your app or website using Paddle.js to let customers buy one-time products and sign up for a subscriptions.
